A good sized rock bass from last summer.
It would have been a nice dinner if the water wasn't so polluted.

Yeah the lake is pretty gross. There's a fair amount of random stuff leaking off of the trains that ends up in the water. However the fishing is excellent. The trout are often pretty finicky though. Some days it's a half dozen, some days it's one or two.
For a polluted lake, it actually sounds pretty diverse

Yeah there's quite a bit of different species in there. All sorts of panfish and bluegill and weird hybrids. Lots of bass of all sizes. Some weird little catfish looking guys in the cove. And some pretty decent trout if you can trick em. Also all sorts of little critters like bull frogs and crawfish. Plus the beaver family I befriended. I'm really going to miss that place.
Damn, that sounds like an amazing place to fish actually. You'd be crazy not to miss it.

Yeah I've spent almost 15 years hanging out down there. But last summer I wanted to improve my bass fishing skills. So I spent 3 days a week or more down there for 6 or 7 hours until dusk. I posted a picture of the bass hole if you're interested.

In my city we have a river that runs through, supposedly a great trout river -- I've only caught like 2 fish out of it, from like 20+ attempts haha

Yeah the water is pretty polluted there so I've always caught and released.

I don't remember exactly what I was using for that one. However my guess would be chartreuse powerbait to get it to float off the bottom, with a chunk of worm.

I've never actually caught anything from my few attempts to fish a river. But I would recommend a roostertail, try different patterns until you find what they're feeding on. Also, it's all about the location with a river. Look for pools and an slower running off shoots where the fish can rest. I recently moved to a city with a pretty major river running through the center of it. This season I get to learn how to fish out of a river as well. So perhaps we'll be able to swap some tips.
